To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the magnetized electron?photons scattering is a new mechanism for the production of the CMB polarization, the magnetized electron-photon scattering is a new contribution to the tensor modes, the magnetized electrons-photon scattering is also a new source term for the vector modes, the magnetization of the electrons-photon scattering does contribute to the tensor modes and the vector modes, as well as to all the polarization modes of the CMB,
magnetic fields contribute to the last electron-photon scattering, and the magnetic fields with arbitrary orientation and in the presence the relativistic fluctuations are included.

(i) the magnetic field contribution to the electron?photon last scattering is not negligible, (ii) the magnetic field orientation and photon direction are correlated, (iii) the magnetic fields do affect the propagation of relic gravitons, (iv) the magnetic field fluctuations do contribute to the scalar and vector modes, (v) the magnetic fields can be considered as a source of relic gravitrons and relic vectors and (vi) the magnetic fields with arbitrary orientation can be consistently accounted for
In summary, our research is concerned with
the magnetized electron? photon scattering in a curved background and in the presence, in addition, of a scalar, vector and/or a tensor field.
the effects of the relativistic magnetic fields on the cosmic microwave anisotropy and polarization.
the propagation of the relic vector and tensor modes in the presence of a magnetized electron?positron plasma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnetic field contribution to the electron?photon last scattering is a small effect which, however, is worth being investigated in detail.
, for the last scattering of the photons, magnetic fields do indeed contribute to the last electron-photon scattering and to the scalar, tensor and vector modes.
the magnetic field contribution to the electron?photon interaction is negligible at the level of precision of the current CMB experiments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnetic fields do not contribute to the last electron-photon scattering in a way that would affect the cosmic microwave anisotropies on large scales.
the magnetic field contribution to the electron?photon interactions is important in the last scattering surface of the cosmic microwave background.
the magnetized electron?photons scattering does not contribute to the scalar and tensor modes of matter perturbations, but it does to the vector modes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the presence of a magnetized medium, the polarization of the relic radiation is not only determined by the polarization of the magnetic field but also by the polarization of relic gravitons and relic vectors.
, in the presence of magnetic fields, the last scattering surface (LSS) is not a perfect sphere, as it would be in the case of pure electron?photon interaction.
the last scattering surface is magnetized, and that the relic magnetic field is a source of the relic vector and relic graviton modes.
